alt: Table declaring the NHIS 2024 release: universe, weights, strata and PSU counts, rule-of-thumb degrees of freedom, the lonely-PSU rule, pooling, series breaks, and known traps.
note: Provenance: design.json = machine-readable manifest field; design.json notes = the manifest's free text; producer = documentation read 2026-09-10; computed = counted from the store by build.py; book guidance = editorial, not a producer rule.

rows.value: NHIS 2024 (IPUMS NHIS, YEAR = 2024), fielded under the 2016–2025 sample design
Civilian noninstitutionalized population of the United States
SAMPWEIGHT; sample-adult/child module weight (module items incl. SMOKESTATUS2, K6); PERWEIGHT for all-person items

PERWEIGHT for 1997-2018 (all-person core items); PERWEIGHT is not released for 2019+ where the public file contains only sample adults + sample children whose SAMPWEIGHT sums to the full civilian noninstitutionalized population — full-population series use PERWEIGHT pre-2019 and SAMPWEIGHT 2019+

The final annual weight includes design, ratio, nonresponse, and calibration adjustments; calibration controls are age by sex, age by race and ethnicity, education, housing tenure, and region by MSA status
Taylor linearization (variance_tier: taylor), PSUs treated as sampled with replacement
STRATA and PSU (NCHS names PSTRAT and PPSU): 52 strata and 662 PSUs, but only 108 distinct PSU codes, reused across strata
PSU ids repeat across strata: ALWAYS treat (STRATA, PSU) as the clustering key — using PSU alone silently miscomputes variance.
610 by the rule PSUs − strata. NCHS notes that the rule is not directly applicable to the NHIS design; a normal approximation may be adequate when a variable is spread across most clusters

center (deviations from grand mean, equivalent to R survey option survey.lonely.psu='adjust'); decision recorded per playbook §6 — annual full-file designs have ≥2 PSUs per stratum, singletons can arise only in small domains. Every stratum of the full 2024 file has at least 5 PSUs
persons outside the sample-adult/child modules carry SAMPWEIGHT=0

rows.source: design.json; producer: NCHS; computed from data
rows.value: Weights: divide each weight by the number of years pooled (NCHS); means and their Taylor SEs are invariant to this uniform rescaling. Variance: years within one NCHS sample design period (with unchanged public-use design variables) re-sample the same PSUs, so the pooled data are treated like one year with a larger sample -- the same (STRATA, PSU) in different years is ONE cluster; treating those years as statistically independent gives standard errors that are too small. Different sample design periods are statistically independent and need distinct strata. IPUMS STRATA embed a design-period indicator and are constant within a period, so pooled views key clusters as design period + STRATA + PSU (pooled_variance_groups). Sources: NCHS, Variance Estimation and Other Analytic Issues in the 1997-2005 NHIS (Nov 2009), pp. 4, 10-12, 15, https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/nchs/data/nhis/9705var.pdf ; NCHS, Variance Estimation Guidance, NHIS 2006-2015 (Jun 2016), pp. 3, 10-12, 15-17, https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/nchs/data/nhis/2006var.pdf ; NCHS, Variance Estimation Guidance, NHIS 2016-2017 (Oct 2018), pp. 1, 3, 8-10, 13, https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/nchs/data/nhis/2016var.pdf ; NCHS, 2019 NHIS Survey Description, pp. 10, 18, 31 (the 2016-2025 sample design continues through the 2019 questionnaire redesign), https://ftp.cdc.gov/pub/Health_Statistics/NCHS/Dataset_Documentation/NHIS/2019/srvydesc-508.pdf ; IPUMS NHIS User Note: Variance Estimation, https://nhis.ipums.org/nhis/userNotes_variance.shtml (verified 2026-09-10). NCHS's 2024 guidance: divide the weight by the number of years pooled and keep PSTRAT and PPSU as they are; 635 of the 662 (STRATA, PSU) pairs of 2024 also appear in 2023

2019: 2019 questionnaire redesign. NHIS content, universes, and weighting redesigned in 2019; NCHS advises caution comparing 2019-forward estimates with earlier years (see nhis_era derived flag). The 2024 sample adds a 25 percent increase in nonmetropolitan households
svy nests PSU codes within the declared strata; R's svydesign stops without nest = TRUE; code that groups or clusters on PSU alone merges unrelated PSUs
